scores.evidence: CRDT (Yjs + y-prosemirror). Every copy ends up identical without the server deciding order. The server relays, checks and stores edits
scores.rationale: Mostly correct on Yjs, durable confirm, and server-side validation; minor imprecision (Yjs markers vs. 'log ≤3× snapshot', Redis pub/sub without routing, validating edits server-side is nontrivial) but no design-breaking errors.

scores.evidence: Rich text: headings, lists, marks, links and images. Works online first, and can survive short offline gaps.
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with explicit deferrals (long offline, comments, E2EE) and realistic buildable scope; merge semantics for structural conflicts are only lightly treated.

scores.evidence: Confirm only after the Postgres commit... Permissions stay strictly consistent: the server is the authority and checks every incoming edit
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear data ownership and honoured choices; minor loose ends like Redis pub/sub vs. per-document routing and persistence path through Hocuspocus.

scores.evidence: Property-based fuzzing (fast-check): 2–20 simulated clients ... messages reordered, duplicated and delayed ... chaos harness kill -9 ... restore drill
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, runs early for the riskiest decision (V1), has labeled provisional thresholds, and continues in production via divergence detector, SLO and canaries.

scores.evidence: If A3 is false (users work offline for days), the default merge choice stays, but Phase 2 grows.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit, numbers labeled ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN, sensitivity and revisit triggers stated, and confirmation path given.

scores.evidence: Divergence detector: clients send a hash of their document state every 30 s; the server compares and alerts on any mismatch.
scores.rationale: Covers crashes, failover, divergence, malformed/oversized edits, revocation, rate limits, Redis loss, XSS links; lacks detail on malicious-yet-valid CRDT updates, poisoned history and recovery from detected divergence.

scores.evidence: Canary deploys: 1 replica first, rolled out further after 30 min clean.
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, kill switch, SLO, on-call and runbooks are concrete and sized to a small team; incident response and schema migration ops are somewhat thin.

scores.evidence: Infra cost per concurrent session | UNKNOWN: finance or product supplies a ceiling; needed before V5
scores.rationale: Cost is a gated input with build-vs-buy trade-off and a V5 cost check, but no drivers, scaling estimates or concrete cost controls are given.

scores.evidence: R3: the stored format and the sync protocol are locked once real documents exist
scores.rationale: Every decision is labeled by reversibility, R3 ones are validated first with exit paths, point of no return is named, and reversible ones are deferred.

scores.evidence: One TypeScript service. The REST and WebSocket sync roles share an image; a background-worker role runs from the same image
scores.rationale: Starts simple with managed services and deferred items; phased gating and heavy ceremony (DPAs, canary, 5 phases, feature flags with Unleash) are slightly much but mostly justified.

scores.evidence: Exit check: V1 and V3 pass. The divergence detector fires on a mismatch planted in staging.
scores.rationale: Walking-skeleton first, dependency-justified phases, specific tasks, checkable exits and explicit flip-on-failure plans let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: CRDT (Yjs + y-prosemirror)... V1 fails → server decides edit order with operational transforms (ShareDB)
Content schema v1 carries a version number; clients below the minimum schema version are rejected at connect
Property-based fuzzing (fast-check): 2–20 simulated clients make random schema-valid edits, with messages reordered, duplicated and delayed
Confirm only after the Postgres commit... keeps the raw log 30 days before deleting
Redis pub/sub between replicas; reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter
Client offline queue in IndexedDB that resends unconfirmed edits; Long offline sessions (days) deferred
checked on the server: on WebSocket connect, on every incoming edit... Revocation closes the session ≤5 s
Per-user undo and redo (Yjs UndoManager); Version-history UI built on the snapshots
Presence and cursors (Yjs awareness; temporary, never stored)
Phase 0 end-to-end slice with 2 replicas; Phase 1 V1 convergence before format spec
~1 MB text with 100k edits of history loads ≤1 s, ≤50 MB memory; 50 editors at the latency budget
Sync protocol and schema versioned in the repo; min-version handshake; V3 old and new clients edit the same document

traps.evidence: Phase 0: Browser: TipTap + Yjs ... second internal user connected to the other server replica
Confirm only after the Postgres commit, using a managed HA database with synchronous replication
Yjs keeps markers for deleted content

note: Strong, risk-ordered plan with sync-first build, early CRDT fuzzing, durability-before-ack, explicit reversibility and assumptions; weaker on rich-text structural merge semantics, scaling/cost detail, and some large-doc/hot-doc handling.
